evals.name: network-monitoring-default-dir
evals.prompt: requirements.md for network-monitoring is approved. Write its design next so we can generate tasks. The platform system design is in the handoff folder. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state it in the file.
evals.expected_output: The skill fixes the output location (alongside requirements.md), the exact six Kiro sections, requirement traceability, typed interfaces, referencing shared components (AuthMiddleware) instead of redesigning them, and a full error list. Requirements 3 and 4 hide design work (consecutive-failure state, disabling the per-monitor schedule) that a shallow design skips.
expectations: design.md is next to requirements.md and has the six sections in order
Kiro format per the skill: Exactly the six sections, each requirement 1-4 traced in Overview, at least one Mermaid diagram, typed TypeScript interfaces, <= 300 lines
Hidden design work in Requirements 3 and 4: Consecutive-failure state is persisted (counter or last-3 RESULT# query) and pause disables the EventBridge Scheduler schedule; 10 s probe timeout designed

Reuses the platform design: Uses the given keys (ACCOUNT#/MONITOR#, GSI1 name uniqueness for the 409, RESULT# with 7-day TTL); AuthMiddleware referenced briefly; ownership check returns 404 for not-owned ids
Error handling and testing breadth: 400, 401/403, 404, 409, 429, 502/503 each with trigger/response/recovery; unit, integration and E2E with concrete cases

scripted_checks.text: design.md is next to requirements.md and has the six sections in order
scripted_checks.check: test -f .kiro/specs/network-monitoring/design.md && python3 -c "import re,sys;t=open('.kiro/specs/network-monitoring/design.md').read();hs=[h.strip().lower() for h in re.findall(r'^##\s+(?:\d+\.\s*)?(.*)$',t,re.M)];want=['overview','architecture','components and interfaces','data models','error handling','testing strategy'];idx=[next((i for i,h in enumerate(hs) if h.startswith(w)),-1) for w in want];sys.exit(0 if -1 not in idx and idx==sorted(idx) else 1)"

evals.name: audit-log-caller-spec-dir
evals.prompt: Requirements for the audit-log feature are approved; our spec dir for this one is specs/audit-log/, not the default location. Write the feature's design so we can move to task generation. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state it in the file.
evals.expected_output: The skill says a caller-supplied spec_dir MUST be used for reads and writes. Beyond placement, the requirements carry design-shaping numbers (5 s write, 400-day retention, newest-first 100 per page, AuditReader role) and a reference to a 'resumed' action that network-monitoring never defines, which the skill says to flag.
expectations: design.md is in the caller's spec_dir, not the default

Requirements turn into concrete design: Capture path meeting 5 s (e.g. DynamoDB Streams on `platform` -> Lambda), 400-day retention (TTL or S3 lifecycle), key design for by-monitor + time range newest-first with Limit 100 and a token
Gaps are flagged: Notes that 'resumed' has no defined operation in network-monitoring, and that no threat model/DynamoDB handoff exists, stating assumptions
Kiro format and traceability: Six sections, Requirement 1 and 2 ACs traced, typed interfaces and data models with field types, AuditReader -> 403
Scope stays on audit-log: MonitorService and AuthMiddleware referenced, not redesigned; no unrequested features (e.g. export, alerting)

scripted_checks.text: design.md is in the caller's spec_dir, not the default
scripted_checks.check: test -f specs/audit-log/design.md && ! test -e .kiro/specs/audit-log/design.md && python3 -c "import re,sys;t=open('specs/audit-log/design.md').read();hs=[h.strip().lower() for h in re.findall(r'^##\s+(?:\d+\.\s*)?(.*)$',t,re.M)];want=['overview','architecture','components and interfaces','data models','error handling','testing strategy'];idx=[next((i for i,h in enumerate(hs) if h.startswith(w)),-1) for w in want];sys.exit(0 if -1 not in idx and idx==sorted(idx) else 1)"
